what: The x^x reduction, proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib: x^x <= 1 on (0, 1] and strictly increasing on [1, oo); for N >= 2, x^x = N has exactly one positive real root, and it is above 1; and for whole numbers 1 <= q <= p, p/q < x iff p^p < N^q·q^p, p/q <= x iff p^p <= N^q·q^p, x < p/q iff N^q·q^p < p^p, x <= p/q iff N^q·q^p <= p^p, with the whole-number bounds at q = 1. That is the step from the root to the integer comparison every verdict of certs/xx-ledger.json rests on; the ledger names the theorem behind each kind of comparison. Every theorem is checked by Lean's kernel in lake build and replayed by Lean's kernel again and by nanoda, an independently written kernel, through Comparator.
campaign: reports/xx.html, the AI-assisted formalization pipeline completed (the operator, 2026-10-31)

theorems.name: XXReduction.selfpow_le_one
theorems.statement: theorem selfpow_le_one {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (h1 : x ≤ 1) : x ^ x ≤ 1

theorems.name: XXReduction.selfpow_strictMonoOn
theorems.doc: x^x is strictly increasing on [1, ∞): for 1 ≤ a < b, a^a ≤ a^b < b^b.
theorems.statement: theorem selfpow_strictMonoOn : StrictMonoOn (fun x : ℝ => x ^ x) (Set.Ici 1)

theorems.name: XXReduction.one_lt_of_selfpow_eq
theorems.doc: A positive root of x^x = N with N > 1 is above 1.
theorems.statement: theorem one_lt_of_selfpow_eq {N x : ℝ} (hN : 1 < N) (hx : 0 < x) (h : x ^ x = N) : 1 < x

theorems.name: XXReduction.exists_selfpow_eq
theorems.doc: For N ≥ 1, x^x = N has a root x ≥ 1: x^x is continuous on [1, N], equal to 1 at 1 and at least N at N.
theorems.statement: theorem exists_selfpow_eq {N : ℝ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) : ∃ x : ℝ, 1 ≤ x ∧ x ^ x = N

theorems.name: XXReduction.existsUnique_selfpow_eq
theorems.doc: For a real N ≥ 2, x^x = N has exactly one positive real root.
theorems.statement: theorem existsUnique_selfpow_eq {N : ℝ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) : ∃! x : ℝ, 0 < x ∧ x ^ x = N

theorems.name: XXReduction.existsUnique_root
theorems.doc: For a whole number N ≥ 2, x^x = N has exactly one positive real root.
theorems.statement: theorem existsUnique_root {N : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) : ∃! x : ℝ, 0 < x ∧ x ^ x = (N : ℝ)

theorems.name: XXReduction.frac_selfpow_pow
theorems.statement:
theorem frac_selfpow_pow (p q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    (((p : ℝ) / q) ^ ((p : ℝ) / q)) ^ q = ((p : ℝ) / q) ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.frac_selfpow_lt_iff
theorems.doc: (p/q)^(p/q) < N exactly when p^p < N^q·q^p, for q ≥ 1 and N ≥ 0.
theorems.statement:
theorem frac_selfpow_lt_iff (p q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) {N : ℝ} (hN : 0 ≤ N) :
    ((p : ℝ) / q) ^ ((p : ℝ) / q) < N ↔ (p : ℝ) ^ p < N ^ q * (q : ℝ) ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.frac_selfpow_le_iff
theorems.doc: (p/q)^(p/q) ≤ N exactly when p^p ≤ N^q·q^p, for q ≥ 1 and N ≥ 0.
theorems.statement:
theorem frac_selfpow_le_iff (p q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) {N : ℝ} (hN : 0 ≤ N) :
    ((p : ℝ) / q) ^ ((p : ℝ) / q) ≤ N ↔ (p : ℝ) ^ p ≤ N ^ q * (q : ℝ) ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.lt_root_iff
theorems.doc: **The reduction, x > p/q.** For N ≥ 2, the positive root x of x^x = N, and whole numbers 1 ≤ q ≤ p: p/q < x exactly when p^p < N^q·q^p.
theorems.statement:
theorem lt_root_iff {N p q : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hq : 0 < q) (hqp : q ≤ p) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : (p : ℝ) / q < x ↔ p ^ p < N ^ q * q ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.le_root_iff
theorems.doc: **The reduction, x ≥ p/q.** For N ≥ 2, the positive root x of x^x = N, and whole numbers 1 ≤ q ≤ p: p/q ≤ x exactly when p^p ≤ N^q·q^p.
theorems.statement:
theorem le_root_iff {N p q : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hq : 0 < q) (hqp : q ≤ p) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : (p : ℝ) / q ≤ x ↔ p ^ p ≤ N ^ q * q ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.root_lt_iff
theorems.doc: **The reduction, x < p/q.** For N ≥ 2, the positive root x of x^x = N, and whole numbers 1 ≤ q ≤ p: x < p/q exactly when N^q·q^p < p^p.
theorems.statement:
theorem root_lt_iff {N p q : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hq : 0 < q) (hqp : q ≤ p) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : x < (p : ℝ) / q ↔ N ^ q * q ^ p < p ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.root_le_iff
theorems.doc: **The reduction, x ≤ p/q.** For N ≥ 2, the positive root x of x^x = N, and whole numbers 1 ≤ q ≤ p: x ≤ p/q exactly when N^q·q^p ≤ p^p.
theorems.statement:
theorem root_le_iff {N p q : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hq : 0 < q) (hqp : q ≤ p) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : x ≤ (p : ℝ) / q ↔ N ^ q * q ^ p ≤ p ^ p

theorems.name: XXReduction.natCast_le_root_iff
theorems.doc: The whole-number bound from below (q = 1): k ≤ x exactly when k^k ≤ N, for k ≥ 1.
theorems.statement:
theorem natCast_le_root_iff {N k : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hk : 1 ≤ k) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : (k : ℝ) ≤ x ↔ k ^ k ≤ N

theorems.name: XXReduction.root_le_natCast_iff
theorems.doc: The whole-number bound from above (q = 1): x ≤ k exactly when N ≤ k^k, for k ≥ 1.
theorems.statement:
theorem root_le_natCast_iff {N k : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hk : 1 ≤ k) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x)
    (hroot : x ^ x = (N : ℝ)) : x ≤ (k : ℝ) ↔ N ≤ k ^ k

notProved: The negative-base convention. Every theorem is about positive reals (Mathlib's Real.rpow); what x^x means for a negative x, and that no negative x is a root worth counting, is a reading of the problem (claimbox/library/selfpower.py), not proved here.

The decider's code. tools/run-xx-ledger.py computes p^p and N^q·q^p with Python's integers and compares them; the Lean theorems say that comparison decides the bracket, and nothing here proves that the Python computes it. Its red controls (planted wrong brackets, mutants) test it; they do not prove it.
The transcendence of the roots (reports/xx.html §3, one) rests on the Gelfond–Schneider theorem, cited; Mathlib at d13f23b7 holds no Gelfond–Schneider theorem, and none is proved here.
The Comparator challenge is generated from our own file (every proof replaced by sorry), so its statement match checks our text against itself.
